title: Finding the card game's own screens
target: Which screens the card game in TCG Card Shop Simulator keeps behind one manager, and what the reveal screen is telling you while a pack is opened.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A deck to look at or edit
A game in progress if you want to practise

steps.do: Start from the manager rather than from a menu, because the card game is held by one.
steps.because: the card game has a manager that holds the table game itself (PlayCardGameManager, m_PlayTableGame)

steps.do: Look for the deck list there.
steps.because: it holds the deck list screen (m_DeckListScreen)

steps.do: Look for the deck edit screen in the same place.
steps.because: it holds the deck edit screen (m_DeckEditScreen)

steps.do: Expect a workbench screen as well.
Read the rules from the game itself rather than from memory.
Watch the reveal screen's value readout while a card is turned over.
steps.because: the reveal screen has a screen group of its own and a card's value has a group and a text (CardOpeningSequenceUI, m_ScreenGrp, m_CardValueTextGrp, m_CardValueText)

steps.do: For a graded card, read the value before and after rather than only the result.
steps.because: a graded card has a value group with a text for before and a text for after (m_GradedCardValueTextGrp, m_GradedCardValueBeforeText, m_GradedCardValueAfterText)

steps.do: Use the two arrows to tell a gain from a loss at a glance.
steps.because: there is a green and a red arrow for the graded card's value (m_GradedCardValueArrowGreen, m_GradedCardValueArrowRed)

commonMistakes: Hunting through menus for a screen the card game's own manager holds.
Reading the graded value after the change without looking at what it was before.
Missing whether a result was a gain or a loss because the arrows were not read.
Learning the rules from memory when the game ships its own rulebook screen.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
